intent: Ten individual lunar-journal tasks compare clear/cloud-blocked pictures, retain time/visible-shape/cloud notes, distinguish reflected sunlight from self-produced light and appearance from removed pieces, contrast observation drawings and explanatory models, retain labels/not-to-scale warnings/incompleteness and reject invented real distances. Fresh journal transfer changes the observer and uses partly correct multi-constraint distractors.
picturePurpose: Original fictional clear/cloud-blocked night-sky panels support opposite visible-outline and obscured-view matching. They illustrate visibility only, not measured phases, dates, light-source evidence or disappearance. Exact claims and labels stay in code.

workshop.title: 做观月记录：所见、解释与模型边界
workshop.instruction: 从清晰和遮挡的画面开始；连接原句核对反光、外观与模型，别把看不见当不存在。

items.label: 先看画面：哪里还能记录月亮轮廓
items.prompt: Which picture shows a Moon shape that can be drawn?
items.answer: Picture A: a visible crescent Moon.
items.reason: 左图能看到月牙轮廓，可记录这幅画里可见的形状；右图被云遮住。插画没有日期，不能用它推算某晚的月相。
items.hint: 先说看到了什么，再查原文怎样解释；看不清、反光和模型局限，要分别核对。
items.material:
LOOKING AT THE MOON CAREFULLY
Our class observed the Moon from a safe viewing place over several evenings. We wrote down the time and the visible shape, and we noted when clouds blocked the view. We did not record a cloudy evening as proof that the Moon had disappeared. The Moon does not produce its own visible light like the Sun; we see sunlight reflected from it. Its changing appearance during a month does not mean that a piece of the Moon is being removed and replaced.
Our teacher asked us to separate observation from explanation. A drawing can record the shape we see, while a model may help us explore why appearances change. The model needs labels and a warning when sizes or distances are not to scale. A small ball beside a lamp is useful for thinking, but it is not a complete copy of the Earth-Moon system. Good exploration includes careful notes, useful models and clear statements about what those models leave out.

Original picture practice (separate from the class journal):
Picture A shows a visible crescent Moon in an unblocked patch of sky.
Picture B shows clouds blocking that part of the view; no Moon shape is visible.
These fictional pictures have no observation dates and do not prove that the Moon disappeared or changed its light source.
The pictures compare visibility, not successive measured lunar phases. The text gives no exact dates, phase periods, sizes or distances.

options.text: Picture B shows clouds blocking that part of the view; no Moon shape is visible.
options.reason: 右图只有遮住视野的云，没有可见月亮轮廓；不能凭空补画成真实观察。

options.text: Picture A shows a visible crescent Moon in an unblocked patch of sky.
options.reason: 左图能看到月牙轮廓，可记录这幅画里可见的形状；右图被云遮住。插画没有日期，不能用它推算某晚的月相。

options.text: The model needs labels and a warning when sizes or distances are not to scale.
options.reason: 模型比例警告不说明两幅天空插画中哪幅能看见轮廓。

sourceArt.alt: 两幅原创虚构夜空插画：左侧可见一弯月牙，右侧云层遮挡同一片天空，看不到月亮轮廓。只比较视野，不给出观测日期，也不表示月球消失。

items.label: 换个条件：云遮挡，该怎样记
items.prompt: Which picture matches a blocked view, rather than a missing Moon?
items.answer: Picture B: record the cloud-blocked view without claiming the Moon disappeared.
items.reason: 右图没有可见轮廓，因为云遮住视野。配上原文did not...proof，就能区分没看见与证明不存在；左图的月牙不能替右图编一条观测形状。

transfer.stem: Which report keeps both the observation and the model honest?
transfer.passage:
A FICTIONAL CLUB JOURNAL
From a safe viewing place, Mei draws the Moon's visible outline on one evening. On another evening, thick cloud blocks the view, so she writes 'view blocked' without inventing an outline or deleting the entry. The teacher uses a labelled ball-and-lamp model to explore appearances and explains that sizes and distances are not to scale. The model leaves out details of the real Earth-Moon system. A drawing records what was seen; a model helps examine an explanation. The class should keep both the observations and the model's limitations clear. No exact dates or distances are supplied.
